## Bonus summary

This optional bonus turns your **whole project into a Quarto website** on GitHub Pages,
at the same URL as the report you published in Milestone 2.

- [ ] Make your project's `_quarto.yml` a website that renders into `docs/`
- [ ] Add a homepage (your `README`), your report (HTML and PDF), an about page, and a GitHub icon in the menu bar
- [ ] Make `make all` build everything, from downloading the data to the website
- [ ] Publish it on GitHub Pages

::: callout-important
## Up to 5 bonus points, for your team

The points go to **Milestone 4** unless you tell us otherwise when you submit.
They can make up for points lost on that milestone, but can't take it above its maximum.
It is due with Milestone 4 (see the [syllabus](../index.qmd#deliverables)),
and we grade it from the same `3.0.0` release, so your Milestone 4 `README` instructions must still work exactly as written.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Readings for this bonus

-   [Introduction to Quarto and GitHub Pages](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/quarto-github-pages.html) (DSCI 521): the same setup, read it again first
-   Quarto: [includes](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/includes.html) and [alt text for figures](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/figures.html#alt-text)
:::

### 1. Turn your project into a website

1.  **Edit `_quarto.yml`** in the root of your repository:
    add `type: website` and `output-dir: docs`, list the website's pages under `render`,
    and add a `website` section with the menu bar (example below).
    Keep your existing `format` settings (such as `embed-resources` and PDF): they still apply to your report.
2.  **Give each new page `format: html`** in its YAML header, so Quarto doesn't also make a PDF of it.
3.  **Add an empty `.nojekyll` file** to the root of your repository (Quarto copies it into `docs/`),
    and add `.quarto/` to your `.gitignore`.
4.  **Clean up the old report:** it now renders to `docs/reports/<your-report>.html` and `.pdf`, with the website's menu bar.
    Delete the old rendered files from `reports/`, and update your `Makefile` and `README` to the new locations.

`quarto render` now renders the whole website;
`quarto render reports/<your-report>.qmd` still renders just the report, and `quarto preview` shows the website as you edit.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Example `_quarto.yml` and folder layout (step 1)

Change the title, the report's file name and the repository URL to your own.

```{.yaml filename="_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: docs
  render:          # keeps files like CONTRIBUTING.md out of the website
    - index.qmd
    - about.qmd
    - reports/<your-report>.qmd

website:
  title: "Your project title"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: reports/<your-report>.qmd
        text: Report
      - href: about.qmd
        text: About
    right:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/UBC-MDS-2026-27/<your-repository>
        aria-label: GitHub repository

# Keep your existing `format:` settings below.
```

Only the new and changed parts are shown:

```
.
├── _quarto.yml           # now a website: renders everything into docs/
├── .nojekyll
├── Makefile
├── README.md
├── index.qmd             # homepage: includes README.md
├── about.qmd             # the team
├── reports/
│   └── <your-report>.qmd
└── docs/                 # the published website (generated, but committed)
    ├── index.html
    └── reports/
        ├── <your-report>.html
        └── <your-report>.pdf
```
:::

### 2. Add the pages

1.  **Homepage (`index.qmd`):** include your `README` instead of copying it, so the homepage stays up to date.
    It needs no `title`: Quarto uses the `README`'s first heading.

    ```{.markdown filename="index.qmd"}
    ---
    format: html
    ---

    {{{< include README.md >}}}
    ```

2.  **About page (`about.qmd`):** for each team member, their name linked to their GitHub profile,
    and a few sentences in their own words (for example, their background and what interests them in data science).
    The site is public, so each person decides what to share. A photo is optional.

3.  **Report:** the **Report** menu item links to its HTML page, and Quarto adds a link to the PDF on that page.
    Link to both versions from your `README` too.
    Give every figure [alt text]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="Alt text is a short written description of an image, read aloud by screen readers for people who cannot see it. Here every figure in your report needs one, set with fig-alt."}:
    the `fig-alt` option on code cells that make figures, or the `fig-alt` attribute on images:

    ```{.markdown}
    ![Feature densities.](../results/figures/densities.png){#fig-densities fig-alt="Density plots of each feature by class."}
    ```

::: callout-warning
## Links in your `README` must work on the website too

The website only publishes its pages, not the rest of your repository.
A relative link such as `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `src/` works on GitHub but breaks on the website, and Quarto doesn't warn you.
Use the full GitHub URL instead (for example, `https://github.com/UBC-MDS-2026-27/<your-repository>/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md`).
:::

### 3. One `make` command builds everything {#make}

Extend your Milestone 4 `Makefile` so that `make all`, from a fresh clone inside your container,
downloads the data, runs your validation checks and the rest of the analysis,
then renders the whole website into `docs/`.
`make clean` removes everything `make all` creates, **including `docs/`**.

1.  Change the rule behind `publish` so it runs `quarto render` instead of copying the report (sketch below).
2.  Remove your old rule that renders the report in `reports/`: the report now renders as part of the website.
3.  List as [prerequisites]{.term tabindex="0" data-tip="Prerequisites (also called dependencies) are the files listed after the colon in a Makefile rule. Make reruns the rule when any of them is newer than the target. Here they are every file the website reads, so the website rebuilds when one changes."} every file the website reads,
    including your `README` and the figures and tables your report shows.
4.  Say in your `README` how to build the website.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Sketch of the `Makefile` changes (step 3)

Change the file names to your own:

```{.makefile filename="Makefile"}
.DELETE_ON_ERROR:

publish: docs/index.html

docs/index.html: _quarto.yml index.qmd README.md about.qmd \
		reports/<your-report>.qmd results/figures/<your-figure>.png
	quarto render

clean:
	rm -rf docs
	# ... and everything else your pipeline creates
```

-   `quarto render` empties `docs/` first, so no old pages are left over.
-   `.DELETE_ON_ERROR:` deletes `docs/index.html` if the render fails partway.
    Without it, the next `make` would find `docs/index.html` and say there is nothing to do.
:::

::: callout-important
## A clean build, with no warnings

Before you submit, run `make clean` and then `make all` inside your container.
Everything should rebuild, and Quarto should print **no `ERROR` or `WARN` messages**
(for example, about links it could not find). Messages from other tools, such as Jupyter, don't count.
We grade the bonus by doing the same.
:::

### 4. Publish on GitHub Pages

1.  Commit `docs/`, including `docs/.nojekyll` (check with `ls -a docs`, and on GitHub.com).
    It is generated, but GitHub Pages can only publish files in your repository.
2.  Keep the GitHub Pages setting from Milestone 2 (`main` branch, `/docs` folder).
    The homepage is now `https://ubc-mds-2026-27.github.io/<your-repository>/`,
    and the report moves to `.../reports/<your-report>.html`.
3.  Update the report link in your `README`, and say in your `README` and in the repository's **About** box
    that the URL is now your project's website.

## Submission instructions

On Gradescope, under the bonus assignment, enter (there is no PDF to make):

1.  the URL of your published website
2.  the URL of your project's GitHub.com repository
3.  the URL of your `3.0.0` release
4.  which milestone the bonus points should go to (Milestone 4 if you leave it blank)

The usual project expectations apply: GitHub flow with reviewed pull requests,
communication in GitHub issues, and meaningful commit messages.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Rubric

You start at 100% (all 5 bonus points) and lose marks for each problem below. Each 20% is 1 bonus point.

| Grade | Problem |
|-------|---------|
| -20% | The website is not published on GitHub Pages from `docs/`, or the menu bar is missing Home, Report, About or the GitHub icon linking to the repository |
| -20% | The homepage copies the `README` instead of including it, or a link in it is broken on the website |
| -20% | The report is not a page of the website in both HTML and PDF, the `Makefile` or `README` still use its old location, or a figure has no alt text |
| -20% | The about page does not introduce each team member |
| -20% | From a fresh clone, inside the container, `make all` does not run the whole analysis and build the website, Quarto prints an `ERROR` or `WARN` message, or `make clean` does not remove everything `make all` creates (including `docs/`) |
:::
